author: reek
body: s0/s1 are callee-saved but excluded: s1 is rv-heap-reg and s0 the memo base, both owned by the tree emitter for the same program. t3 (index ncallee) is the non-crosser pick, not a0, because a0 is both return and arg-zero and one register cannot hold two abstract indices; t0-t2 are the tree emitter's helper temps. a0-a7 sit in arg order so a leaf's entry moves elide.

author: reek
body: budget 26 > 19 allocatable regs on purpose: it sizes the verifier's occupant array, and slack is cheaper than an overflow. diva/divb -1 because rem/div are three-operand and fix no register.

author: reek
body: t5/t6 are never allocated, consumed within one instruction's selection (t5 spilled dest or oversized imm, t6 second operand). Reusing the tree emitter's temp tail is safe: a function is emitted entirely by one path or the other.

author: reek
body: a zero-instruction function has every vreg a parameter, so a LvReg result is an arg-register index and must be < 8

author: reek
body: the >8-param decline is the ABI: a ninth parameter arrives on the caller's stack, not in a register

author: reek
body: opening is declined BY NAME: rv-emit-function-framed appends a print-result epilogue for it, a special case attached to a name that an instruction-shape whitelist cannot see. A selector claiming opening emits a correct function and a silent program.

author: reek
body: a verifier violation DECLINES, not halts: the wire is the only output, there is no diagnostic channel, and the tree emitter is the fallback

author: reek
body: answers -1 for a slot: called only where the location is known to be a register, and -1 keeps a mislabelled slot visible rather than plausible

author: reek
body: LoRem/LoDiv emit NOTHING, not a substitute instruction: they cannot arrive (rv-lir-op-ok excludes them), and a missing instruction makes a whitelist slip visible where a plausible substitute would be a silent miscompile

author: reek
body: a slot destination computes into t5 then stores; t5 may also hold the loaded left operand, safe because the three-operand ALU reads both sources before it writes

author: reek
body: frame capped at 2032: the largest 16-aligned size the signed-12 addi/ld/sd offset fields encode. A larger frame would encode wrong, not diagnose, so it is refused.

author: reek
body: slots at [0, nslots*8), used callee-saved above them; no ra cell, the whitelist admits no call

author: reek
body: the callee-saved pool is handed out lowest-free, so used indices are a prefix and saving [0, nused) saves exactly what the body writes

author: reek
body: the plan is the compiler's (lir-emv-for); this only maps abstract index to register. A cycle stages through nregs -> t5, safe because entry moves precede instruction selection. Runs AFTER the prologue: a slot store needs the frame, a callee-saved move must not precede its save.

author: reek
body: the result is read into a0 BEFORE the epilogue: a callee-saved result must be copied out before the restore overwrites it, a slot result loaded before sp is popped past it

author: reek
body: emits [WCET] lir-handled per selected function: the only signal separating selector from tree output, which answer alike when both are correct

author: fester
body: The RISC-V target descriptor, its physical mapping, and the dispatch that routes a function through the LIR when `rv-lir-selects` admits every construct in it; anything else falls back to `rv-emit-function`. The allocator and both verifiers are the compiler's own, bundled by `-WithLir` and not reimplemented here.
